causal_chain: A single pooled preference vector blurs these tastes and lets dominant/popular patterns overwhelm niche but recurring evidence.
A slot-based history encoder can separate a user's history into a small set of attraction states and exclusion states without using held-out data.
At scoring time, attraction slots recover candidate-aligned support while exclusion slots suppress items that match repeatedly avoided or conflicting patterns.
This separation should improve ranking of items that are consistent with one user intent but diluted by other intents in the same history, improving full-sort NDCG@10.
Users in ML-1M often mix several stable tastes inside one interaction history.

research_spec.competing_explanation: Any gain could come from added capacity and history pooling alone rather than from the explicit attraction-versus-exclusion decomposition; a matched single-branch multi-slot history encoder with similar parameter count could explain the same outcome if the subtractive exclusion relation is unnecessary.
discriminative_predictions: Compared with a matched single-branch history-slot control, the proposed model should rank fewer popularity-heavy but semantically diffuse items in the top-10 for users with long mixed-genre histories.

If the exclusion branch is removed while keeping the same slot encoder and parameter budget, top-ranked lists should become less stable against hard negatives that resemble one historical sub-interest but conflict with the dominant one.
The advantage should be larger for users whose training histories are diverse, because exclusion slots matter most when multiple intents conflict inside one user profile.
expected_evidence: Offline full-sort NDCG@10 exceeds the matched mechanism-off control under the frozen ML-1M protocol.
Per-user gains are concentrated among medium- and long-history users with higher item-cluster diversity in their training interactions.
Top-ranked recommendation lists show reduced overlap with globally popular items when those items are unsupported by any attraction slot and strongly activated by exclusion slots.
research_spec.falsifier: If a matched control that retains the same multi-slot history encoder but removes the exclusion branch and subtractive scoring matches or exceeds NDCG@10, the proposed exclusion relation is not carrying unique value under this protocol.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This is a high-change candidate because it replaces static single-vector user representation with a dual-relation slot-based history encoder, introduces an explicit negative collaborative relation at scoring time, and changes the interaction structure from one direct affinity channel to attraction-minus-exclusion evidence composition.

causal_chain: A disagreement-aware routing gate can detect when direct user-item affinity and prototype-mediated affinity diverge, then selectively trust prototype transport for ambiguous or mixed-interest cases.

An anti-collapse auxiliary objective that discourages all mass concentrating on one prototype keeps the multi-prototype representation functionally active rather than degenerating into standard matrix factorization.
Representing each item as a mixture over shared collaborative prototypes lets the scorer compare users and items at the facet level rather than only through one global dot product.
Representing each user as a sparse mixture over several latent preference prototypes preserves separable intent components instead of averaging them away.
Together these changes should recover hard positives whose relevance is tied to one user facet, improving full-sort NDCG@10 under pairwise training.
Users in ML-1M often express multiple stable but partially conflicting taste facets that a single embedding compresses together.

causal_chain: A candidate-conditioned history router can select a sparse support subset and a sparse suppression subset from the user's interacted items instead of collapsing history into one static user vector.
Because full-sort ranking evaluates many near-neighbor items, item-specific retrieval over history should especially help hard comparisons where static collaborative embeddings blur multiple intents.

If this routed evidence is genuinely useful rather than just extra capacity, gains should concentrate on users with longer or more diverse histories and on candidates whose top supporting history items are few and high-confidence.

The support path raises scores when a candidate aligns with a coherent local taste pattern, while the suppression path lowers scores when the candidate mainly matches historically conflicting or popularity-driven evidence.

research_spec.competing_explanation: Any measured gain could come from increased scorer flexibility or higher effective item-item capacity rather than from candidate-conditioned support/suppression routing itself.

causal_chain: A small bank of persistent user preference states can separately store distinct collaborative intents extracted from the user's training interactions.
Because full-sort ranking must distinguish hard positives from nearby substitutes, candidate-specific state selection should recover held-out items that are diluted under single-vector scoring.
Item-conditioned routing over those states lets each candidate be compared against the most relevant latent intent instead of an averaged preference vector.
State transport over the user's observed training-time interaction order preserves which intents co-activate and how later interactions refine earlier ones.
Therefore a multi-state transport recommender should improve NDCG@10 over a matched single-state pairwise control, especially for users with diverse histories.
Users with mixed-taste histories are poorly summarized by a single static embedding.
research_spec.closest_parent: A recommender that models each user as a small set of persistent latent preference states and updates those states through pairwise event-conditioned memory transport will better capture mixed and shifting tastes than single-embedding models, yielding higher full-sort NDCG@10 under the same offline pairwise protocol.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any observed gain may come from increased parameter count or generic regularization from attention-style pooling rather than from persistent multi-state transport and candidate-conditioned routing.
discriminative_predictions: If transport is causal, ablating chronological state updates while keeping the same number of states and parameters should hurt more on users with longer histories than on short-history users.
Relative improvement should be larger for users whose training histories are more interaction-diverse than for users with narrow homogeneous histories.
Replacing candidate-conditioned routing with uniform averaging over states should substantially reduce or erase any gain if routing is the real mechanism.
expected_evidence: A matched single-state control under the same pairwise protocol underperforms the multi-state transport model on full-sort NDCG@10.
Mechanism-off ablations localize the effect: both no-routing and no-transport variants lose most of the frontier model's advantage.
User-stratified evaluation shows the largest deltas in medium/high diversity history buckets rather than only in head-popularity buckets.
research_spec.falsifier: The hypothesis is falsified if the multi-state transport model fails to beat its matched single-state control, or if any gain remains unchanged after removing candidate-conditioned routing and chronological state transport, indicating the proposed mechanism is not carrying the effect.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This candidate changes the core user representation from one static embedding to a set of persistent latent states, changes the interaction structure by making scoring candidate-conditioned through routing, and adds a custom train-time state transport capability over each user's observed history. These are not parameter tweaks or wrappers around the active profile families.
research_spec.hypothesis: A candidate-local GeneralRecommender that represents each user as a small set of persistent latent preference states, updates those states by train-history transport, and scores each item through candidate-conditioned routing over the state bank will achieve better full-sort NDCG@10 than matched single-state pairwise collaborative filtering because it can preserve and selectively activate distinct intents instead of collapsing them into one average user vector.

research_spec.minimal_testable_wedge: The smallest isolatable wedge is candidate-conditioned routing over a fixed-size bank of persistent user states built from training histories, compared against the same backbone with one pooled user embedding and no routing.

causal_chain: A parallel exclusion mixture built from contrastive pressure against sampled negatives can encode which prototype directions the user history tends to reject.

Better separation between attraction and exclusion channels should improve the ordering of held-out positives in full-sort ranking, especially for mixed-interest users and substitute-heavy neighborhoods.
Learning a small shared bank of item prototypes lets items expose reusable collaborative facets beyond single embeddings.
Routing each user history into an adaptive mixture over prototypes creates a target-agnostic multi-intent preference state that can preserve distinct tastes within one user.

Scoring candidates by combining direct affinity, positive prototype transport, and subtractive exclusion pressure should promote items aligned with one active taste while suppressing misleading globally popular or cross-taste candidates.
User histories in ML-1M often mix multiple stable tastes, so collapsing them into one user vector blurs intent.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any observed gain could come from increased parameter count or auxiliary regularization rather than from disagreement-aware prototype routing and exclusion transport specifically.
discriminative_predictions: Ablating only the exclusion channel while keeping positive prototype transport should disproportionately hurt cases where sampled negatives are near substitutes of positives.
Compared with matched BPR_MF, the candidate should show larger ranking gains for users whose train histories are diverse across item neighborhoods than for users with highly coherent histories.

If gains are merely due to extra capacity, a mechanism-off version with equalized parameter count but no prototype routing should recover most of the benefit; if not, the full mechanism should remain distinctly better.

Prototype assignment entropy should be lower for focused users and higher for mixed-interest users; if routing is mechanistically useful, this variance should correlate with per-user ranking improvement.
expected_evidence: Exclusion-channel ablation loses more on hard-negative-sensitive users than on globally easy users.

Prototype usage statistics are non-collapsed, with multiple prototypes receiving meaningful mass across users and items.
research_spec.falsifier: If the full model fails to outperform both matched BPR_MF and its mechanism-off ablation, or if learned prototype routing collapses to a single prototype for nearly all users/items, the hypothesis is not supported.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This proposal changes the core representation from single user/item embeddings to shared prototype mixtures with explicit dual attraction-exclusion transport, adds a new interaction structure through disagreement-aware routing, and introduces custom executable capabilities absent from the active profile catalog. It is not a parameter tweak or wrapper on existing BPR_MF or LightGCN variants.
